Reviewed commits: `c347ff8bb74e78062c3ae8162c8a0e9a2074f398`,

Method: read-only review of the production diff and receiving paths.
No analyzer, build, test, Java, JFR or heap process was started by this audit.

Result: **No hidden or unselected major semantic change was found in this diff.**
This is a source-scope audit. It does not replace the formal model, test gates or
closed-project source/sink comparison. The parent has the test receipts: 2,058
core tests and 445 JVM tests, with no failure, error or skipped test.

| Requirement | Current source and result |
|---|---|
| Ignore abstract STAR demand field E | `normalizeDemandFieldExclusion` is unchanged and clears E only on abstract STAR demand. Actual E and concrete demand E still constrain admitted descent. `RestrictedInitialPolicy.emit`, `canEmitInitial`, `insideDemand` and C5 use that normalization. No global E erasure was added. |
| Run-2 requested STAR; later no outgoing FLOW STAR demand | Run-aware `RestrictedInitialPolicy` accepts a proper descendant under STAR only at run-2. `DemandStore.validateIncoming` rejects later FLOW STAR entries. Engine `RunConfig` supplies actual run, direction and limit. `retainSummary` and `HandOff` assert ANY/Empty-E restricted FLOW demand conclusions; they do not silently coerce export. |
| One-step ANY refinement and mark mismatch | The first counted field stops refinement; classes do not consume budget and the static class+field anchor is indivisible. The selected concrete exact-first-field exception remains. A concrete U demand rejects T. GROUP selectors bind a compatible full atom through the current mark table. |
| C2/C5 consistency | C5 uses `canStoreInitial`: a legal raw emitter image plus raw containment, or the exact raw preimage of a canonical FLOW STAR key. It does not use self-emission idempotence. `restrictPlainFacts` normalizes selected FLOW pieces before GroupKey merge and coverage. |
| Abstract EXACT read barrier | `EdgeApplication.flow` does not promote an EXACT ancestor across an ordinary field read. Only the existing excluded identity keep identifies the field-preserve effect. `nearLeafViews` omits EXACT ancestors. |
| Latent write E and canonical summary boundary | EXACT/FLOW results can hold E. Strong writes retain it, including nested inner ANY/DEMAND residuals. `retainSummary` normalizes complete pairs before raw storage/publication; only pure FLOW EXACT endpoints change to STAR. Point MethodEdgeStore initials stay raw. TAINT, ZERO, ND and exact class markers do not normalize. |
| Definite MUST | Abstract MUST matching requires actual MUST coverage; STAR/MAY/EXACT are insufficient. Forward native abstract MUST views are transient ANY/DEMAND results, with their old output E on the STAR read. Backward MUST initials remain invalid. |
| Whole-position RemoveAll | Null-mark `Cleaner` requires AT_AND_BELOW. JIR rejects terminal AnyField all-mark removal and accepts roots/named fields. Direct FLOW kill residuals use the same write-style exclusion/inner-demand contract. Selected-mark cleaners remain separate. This is an explicitly selected semantic change, not a technical optimization. |
| Backward ZERO | `published` keeps the exact preexisting `!forward && premise.isZero` bypass. The native backward-ZERO-premise exclusion remains. No stop-policy or seed-routing change was added. |
| Run-1 has no ND executable edge | `checkPremise` still requires `InitialAp` in run-1. No run-1 origin/conjunction/predicate store file changed in these commits. Later ND handling is unchanged. |
| Run-1 field policy and statics | Run1Abstraction, static service, point resume, writer registration, static pool, static result routing, and source replay code are unchanged. The field-write condition extends typed support for newly legal tails; run-1 still emits only its old initials and clears E on demotion. No weak-write policy is introduced. |
| No grounding/source rewrite | No grounding support type, source guard support, source replay channel, actual-input grounding test, MarkTable change, condition rewrite, rule identity change or MethodEdgeStore metadata was added. |
| Canonical keys at secondary boundaries | RunSummaryStore, publication index and native record storage assert canonical FLOW. Killed static writes retain raw observation keys and normalize only guidance/survivor comparisons. Predefined schema is already structurally canonical: only ZeroIdentity and PrefixFlowIdentity exist; it cannot express FLOW EXACT endpoints. Instantiated predefined results are unchanged. |
| Candidate delivery in both orders | PublicationIndex and CalleeSubscriptions both include concrete STAR descendant candidates. The final AP matcher applies exact mark/E/tail tests. This implements the selected demanded STAR case; it does not broaden arbitrary concrete ANY/MUST candidates. |
| C5 fixed-right work removal | Mapped states test their real output label before graph-owner lookup/decoding/enqueue. FLOW states stay eligible because a mapped predecessor can repair their mark. Source/writer preflight is unfiltered. Composition retains the old anchor/overlap and full/group compatibility law. C2 uses the existing unfiltered view path. |

False is stored only after a normal completed answer. Local-only tests, outside-graph short circuit and output labels remain unchanged. No cross-query answer cache is present. |

Production scope is 28 files. New helpers are the run-aware admission policy,
FLOW summary normalizer and internal C5 filter capability. Statistics add
counter observations only; they do not enter fact, method, rule, group or
publication equality. Default scalar/reference APIs choose a forward policy so
MUST template tests can use them. Actual engine C2 and C5 receive the real
`RunConfig.admissionPolicy`; no engine call to these operations uses that default.

The campaign can change final observations because admission and summary semantics
are explicitly selected changes. Do not describe all three commits as semantics-
preserving speed optimizations. Only fixed-right pruning and per-view memo are

source audit nor green unit tests establish no FN for incomplete project runs.

# Final review of the next-iteration proposals

Date: 29 October 2026.
Reviewed runtime: `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`.
Documents:

- `docs/design/bidirectional-demand-refinement-next-iteration-20261029.md`
- `docs/design/bidirectional-static-demand-row-selection-20261029.md`

Evidence: current source, the closed 30-window JFR summary, the embedded current
native-profile evidence, and task.md. No runtime edit, build, test, analyzer or
new reader was run for this review.

Result: **PASS for proposal-stage scope and required proof gates. No concrete semantic contradiction was found.**
Their union, schedule and visibility equivalence proofs remain implementation
gates. This review does not claim that those proofs are complete.

## Two clarifications verified in the final text

1. **The SCC family universe must include both Owners construction sites.**
   `FrozenStaticCompletion.Builder.build` creates Owners for every bridge label
   and again for each projected entry row. The proposed abstract
   `for (family in ownerFamilies)` must enumerate both sets, with every stable
   family ID in `[0,F)`. Iterating only bridge labels would leave some C2 entry
   family bits unset and could omit initial admission. The main proposal and
   detailed SCC section now explicitly name both family sources. This resolves
   the earlier ambiguity. Preserve each projected entry family's existing union
   of owners in the implementation.

2. **Protection containment means exact physical membership.**
   In the new exact-header helper, `mergeOrdinary` must mean structural
   `taintAlg.mergeAdd`, not a ConclusionGroup/subsumption operation. A broad ANY
   relation can semantically cover an exact dependency without containing its
   exact `(path, tail, mark)` node. Such coverage does not prove mask containment.
   The safe helper takes two valid same-header trees and constructs their exact
   ordinary union and pointwise mask OR. Keep it internal; do not expose a
   general root/mask unchecked setter. Preserve validation for subtraction,
   projection, cleaner/transfer changes, cross-header compaction and every other
   narrowing operation. The delta proof must retain
   `deltaRoot = ordinaryDelta union protectedDelta`, including annotation-only
   updates. Section2.2 now explicitly
   names structural coordinate containment and `taintAlg.mergeAdd`. This resolves
   the earlier ambiguity.

Both scope clarifications are present in the final documents. Neither changes
the intended behavior or requires a new semantic decision. Neither describes a
discovered defect in the current committed analyzer.

## Static selector checks

- The direct FLOW ordinal is safe. A packed bridge geometry has one unique
  `0L` label at most. Its own owner family is retained. Dropped colored owner
  queries cannot change the Boolean of later pure reachability questions;
  they only change scratch progress and diagnostics.
- FULL/GROUP direction is correct. Output coverage of a full T selects exact T
  and its covering GROUP. Output coverage of GROUP G selects GROUP G, not
  arbitrary full atoms in G. Symmetric composition with GROUP G additionally
  selects full rows in G. Two different full T/U atoms in one group remain
  incompatible. The full input/output pair is retained for every ordinal.
- FLOW repair is retained. Mapped predecessors can color a FLOW right state.
  Fixed mapped right states retain their final right mark. The source/writer
  preflight is deliberately not filtered as if its immediate mark were final.
- Nullable ZERO selectors remain distinct from group IDs and wildcards. Bridges
  have no ZERO endpoint; local W/R rows can. A right ZERO endpoint must remain
  canonical. A mapped state with ZERO at its left does not enter a static
  predecessor traversal. `groupOf(ZERO)` remains invalid.
- The mapped-geometry precheck is conservative in its stated FULL scope.
  Replacing a compatible mapped required mark Q with the original member's M
  preserves concrete-kind geometry and E, while making the rendered-mark test
  reflexive. Therefore every productive old mapped row has the precheck
  witness. The code retains FLOW and falls back for unproved ZERO/other cases.
- C2 early mark selection is a necessary condition of the unchanged emitter.
  The full emitter still checks field E, tail, path, budget and static grammar.
  Geometry placeholder normalization is correctly delayed until the real mark
  is restored. Coverage envelopes must retain every possible emitter family,
  as the proposal explicitly requires.
- Local W/R attachments retain exact MethodKey ownership. Shared B visibility
  remains common-method based. Indexing mark selectors does not merge those
  scopes or turn a full atom into a group.

## SCC visibility checks

The proposed recurrence follows caller-to-callee edges. Each SCC first contains
its own family-owner bits, so self paths and recursion are retained. Child unions
in reverse topological order give exactly the current reflexive transitive
visibility predicate. A graph-indexed method cannot equal an outside-graph owner
under the same CommonMethod equality. An absent root retains only direct
outside-owner membership. It gains no invented outgoing edge.

The table is immutable before concurrent reads and is released with the run2
completion snapshot. Local owner equality and exact-context W/R lookups do not
use the transitive table. No method demand closure or static edge product is
materialized. The payload arithmetic is correct: `51,953 * 257 * 8 =
106,815,368` bytes before headers and DAG/outside-owner data. The edge-word bound
is `117,581 * 257 = 30,218,317`, with SCC/build costs still separate.

Whole TB2 Java evidence supports this high-priority stage: call-graph membership
is 47.68% of Java samples and 50.94% of sampled allocation weight. The exact gain
remaining after row selection is not known. Both documents keep that measurement
gate and do not require an unnecessary eager table.

## Union and scheduling checks

The protection-union candidate preserves flags rather than removing them. Its
scope is exact-header monotone union. The separate delta proof and retained
narrowing validation are necessary and correctly called out. Ordinary Facts
comparison omits protection, so annotation-only updates must not be deduplicated.

Joined writer input selection is output-independent in the current source:
`visitJoinedCandidates` and `matches` use the complete writer premise, not its
output. Grouping those visits by exact owner/original can retain all scalar output
applications. The proposal keeps raw mx, ZERO guards, complete input deduplication,
recursive callbacks, killed writers and guide-only results. It does not confuse
immediate static supply with summary/guidance binding.

Pending input replay, publication packing and changed-fact packing are schedule
changes. The documents do not assume that a leaf-union lemma proves the entire
engine. They require complete stateful rule/ND saturation, input-alias closure,
identity/effect splitting, registration-before-delay, all publication/input arrival
orders, detached reentrant work and Work reservations. Full keys preserve caller
context, call stage, layer, header and complete premise. The changed-fact design
keeps control and unchanged lanes. No unsupported convergence claim is made.

## Evidence and impact claims

The documents separate the late native and whole-run Java sample denominators.
They do not sum inclusive shares. The 412.7 million fixed rejects are correctly
identified as repeated predicate failures with both mark and geometry causes.
The 41.64 GB memo payload is cumulative allocation; the 2,006.675 GiB JFR figure is
sampled allocation weight. Neither is called retained heap.

The native Stirling protection evidence confirms 28.35% mask membership and the
specified 12.85%/11.52% store-context subsets. Whole-run Java protection shares
are different observations and are presented as such. The proposal distinguishes
removable union validation from required transfer-mask work.

The finite 100-to-1 examples describe operation counts in their stated scope.
The documents expressly withhold a 2x project claim until actual mergeability,
selected-label ratios, owner-query counts and complete engine times are measured.
The current missing baseline locations are not silently fixed through any of
these candidates. Source-output reset, field processing, rule conditions and the
backward ZERO exception remain outside this iteration's proposed changes.
